description_full: SOLV Energy, Inc. provides infrastructure services to the power industry in the United States. It offers engineering, procurement, construction, testing, commissioning, operations, maintenance, and repowering services. The company engages in designing, building, and maintaining utility-scale solar and battery storage projects, substation foundations, civil construction, and related transmission and distribution infrastructure. It also provides operations and maintenance services. The company serves project developers, independent power producers, and utilities. SOLV Energy, Inc. was founded in 2008 and is headquartered in San Diego, California.

financial_summary: SOLV Energy, Inc. is a mid-cap utilities business with a $5.2B market cap on $2.5B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +3.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 10% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 10% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $310M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.22× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -10.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 3.7×.

Shareholder yield is only 1.8%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
